question.text: In the 20th century, this Southern Hemisphere country built a nearly 3500-mile fence to keep dingos, a type of wild dog that lives in this country's outback, out of its more populated southeast.
question.clue: This country's longest serving prime minister was Robert Menzies, who founded its Liberal Party and famously called the middle class, "The Forgotten People".

swap.leadin: Descendents of convicts known as "currency lads" carried out raids on feral horses called brumbies in the bush and this region.
swap.text: Name this region where jackaroos established "cattle empires" around stations. The disastrous Emu War occurred in this rural region of central Australia.
swap.clue: An overland telegraph line through this region was scouted by Robert Burke and William Wills but was eventually built through Alice Springs.

question.text: The "history wars" began after the Bringing Them Home report was released on these people. This term refers to Australian Aborigines taken from their families as children by the Australian government.
question.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

swap.leadin: This colony was founded by the First Fleet on January 26, 1788, and its first governor was Arthur Phillip.
swap.text: Name this colony which originated around Port Jackson. Lachlan Macquarie was the final governor of this territory.
swap.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the failure of the Gallipoli Campaign.
question.text: The date of the Gallipoli landing is a day of remembrance for this expeditionary force, which was composed of soldiers from two British commonwealths.
question.answerHtml: ANZAC [or the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps]
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.leadin: Australia has struggled with the civil rights of these people.
swap.text: These indigenous Australians were frequently massacred at the beginning of British colonization of Australia.
swap.clue: Over two dozen of these people were killed in the Myall Creek Massacre, which took place not long after the Black War against these people.

question.leadin: As Treasurer of Australia, this man oversaw the creation of the Australian Dollar and later ended the pegging of the currency to the British pound.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister who more famously went missing while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967. Ironically, a swimming pool in Melbourne was named in his honor.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.leadin: Peter Lalor was one leader of this event, and each of its thirteen participants who were tried for treason were acquitted.
swap.text: Name this rebellion by gold miners against the British colonial administration of Victoria.
swap.answerHtml: Eureka Stockade [or Eureka Rebellion; accept equivalents for “Rebellion” such as “Revolt”]
swap.clue: It was partly incited by the acquittal of James Bentley, whose hotel was burned to the ground, leading Robert Rede to request additional troops from Charles Hotham, whose dispatches are a key source on this event.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This Australian prime minister began dismantling White Australia in 1966, a year before his mysterious disappearance during a swimming incident while in office.
question.clue: A king of this name served under George Maniakes in the Varangian Guard, but was later imprisoned for stealing imperial plunder.

swap.leadin: Following this event, Lachlan Macquarie was appointed governor of a certain colony.
swap.text: Name this rebellion, caused by James MacArthur's importation of the titular alcoholic drink.
swap.clue: When the target of the order disregarded it, George Johnson disobeyed a request to aid in the target's arrest, instead leading a group of men to Government House to overthrow the order's issuer.

question.text: In some Commonwealth countries, the monarch is represented by this position's holder. In Australia, the holder of this position has the power to dismiss the PM and dissolve government.
question.answerHtml: Governor-General [do not accept or prompt on partial answers]
question.clue: John Kerr controversially exercised the formal power to dismiss Whitlam as this executive representative of the monarchy in Australia.

swap.text: One of the most famous people from Victoria was this leader of the Greta Mob. This man killed three policemen at Stringybark Creek and also dictated the Jerilderie Letter.
swap.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

question.leadin: A key controversy in the history wars is over whether the separation of families from children described by this adjective constitutes genocide.
question.text: Give the adjective commonly used to describe those "generations" of children, the subjects of the report Bringing Them Home.

swap.text: The Parramatta River is the major tributary of Port Jackson, the natural harbor of this city in the Southern Hemisphere where you can find the masterpiece of Jorn Utzon.
swap.clue: This city is the largest to be served by the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Scheme, whose construction caused its country to ease pro-white immigration policies.

question.text: A landmark 1891 sheep shearers' strike led to the founding of this party under the "Tree of Knowledge." This party's later leaders included Billy Hughes and Gough Whitlam.
question.answerHtml: Australian Labor Party [or ALP; prompt on Labor Party with “of what country?”]
question.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

swap.text: Menzies built credit among the middle class by calling them by this name, which titles a notable 1942 speech he made emphasizing his connections to ordinary people.

question.text: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.
question.clue: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.

swap.leadin: An incredibly strong worker known as Crooked Mick appears in folktales about a mythical one of these places called the Speewah.
swap.text: Name these places, such as Anna Creek and Victoria Downs. Subsidiaries of these places, prefixed with the word "out-," also name remote communities of Aboriginal Australians.
swap.answerHtml: stations [accept cattle stations; accept sheep stations; accept outstations; prompt on cattle ranches]

question.text: The shootout where Kelly was captured occurred in this small town in Northeast Victoria. A plan to derail train carrying policemen was foiled by the efforts of hostage Thomas Curnow.
question.clue: Kelly was captured in a shootout with police in this town in Victoria.

swap.leadin: Matthew Brady, not to be confused with the American photographer, was known as a "gentleman" one of these people and was an enemy of Governor George Arthur. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this group of outlaws that included Ned Kelly.
swap.clue: "Bolters" like John "Black" Caesar made up the first generation of this profession, whose later practitioners included Mary Ann Bugg and her lover, Captain Thunderbolt.
